column1: # Book 4 review (Fable, 2026-10-30). Finding 4.1266 accepted (semina is the subject of sumere). 4.1215-1216: mutuus ardor is the subject and semina the object of conflixit; the draft had the seeds dashing. 4.1233 and 4.1246 (20-syllable outlier) shortened to the band.

column2: when, the seeds being stirred through the limbs by the goads of Venus,
a mutual ardor, breathing as one, has dashed them together,
Nor do divine powers bar any man from generative sowing,
or cannot pierce the places as well, or, once it has pierced,
wives conceive the more, because so the seeds can take their places,
